title: Timing Reference High Resolution Signal A Too Many Pulses
plain: The fine-detail timing signal A that the computer uses to time spark and fuel precisely is seeing more pulses than it should, often from electrical noise. It usually comes from a crankshaft or distributor sensor.

causes.name: Faulty crankshaft or distributor position sensor
Damaged wiring or connector in the signal circuit
Electrical interference from ignition wires, an aftermarket accessory or a bad ground
Damaged tone ring or sensor disc
Engine computer fault

checks: Inspect sensor wiring and grounds, and keep ignition wires away from it
Test the sensor signal with a scope
fix: Usually a new crank or distributor sensor, or a wiring or ground repair.

title: Glow Plug Sense Circuit
plain: On a diesel, there's a fault in the circuit the computer uses to monitor the glow plugs. Glow plugs heat the cylinders so the engine starts easily in the cold.
symptoms: Check engine light and often a glow plug warning light
White smoke and rough running right after a cold start

causes.name: Damaged or corroded glow plug wiring or connectors
Faulty glow plug control module
Failed glow plug
Engine computer fault

checks: Inspect glow plug wiring and connectors for corrosion or damage
Test each glow plug's resistance and the control module output
fix: Usually a wiring repair or a new glow plug control module; replace any failed glow plugs found during testing.

title: Glow Plug/Heater Circuit "A"
plain: On a diesel, the computer found a problem in glow plug (or intake heater) circuit A. Glow plugs heat the cylinders so the engine starts easily, so expect hard cold starts.
symptoms: Check engine light and often a glow plug warning light
Hard starting or long cranking in cold weather
White smoke and rough running right after a cold start
Engine may not start at all in very cold weather

causes.name: One or more failed glow plugs
Faulty glow plug control module or relay
Damaged, corroded or loose glow plug wiring
Blown fuse or fusible link in the glow plug circuit
Engine computer fault

checks: Test each glow plug's resistance to find any that have burned out
Inspect glow plug wiring, connectors and fuses
Check that the control module or relay powers the plugs when commanded
fix: Most often replacing failed glow plugs, the glow plug control module, or damaged wiring.
examples: Seen on glow-plug diesels such as Ford Power Stroke pickups and VW TDI models

title: Glow Plug/Heater Indicator Circuit
plain: On a diesel, there's a fault in the circuit for the dashboard light that tells you to wait for the glow plugs before starting. The glow plugs themselves may be fine.
symptoms: Wait-to-start or glow plug light stays off, stays on, or flickers
Engine usually starts and runs normally

causes.name: Burned-out indicator bulb or instrument cluster fault
Damaged wiring in the indicator circuit
Engine computer fault

checks: See whether the glow plug light comes on briefly at key-on
Inspect the indicator circuit wiring and cluster connector
fix: Repair the indicator wiring, bulb or instrument cluster.

title: Glow Plug Control Module Control Circuit Low
plain: On a diesel, the signal the engine computer uses to command the glow plug control module is reading too low, so the glow plugs may not switch on.

causes.name: Damaged or shorted wire between the engine computer and glow plug module
Faulty glow plug control module
Engine computer fault

checks: Inspect glow plug wiring, connectors and fuses
Check that the control module or relay powers the plugs when commanded
fix: Repair the control wiring or replace the glow plug control module.

title: Crankshaft Position Sensor "B" Circuit
plain: The engine computer says there's a fault in the circuit for crankshaft position sensor B, a second crank sensor used on some engines. Crank sensor problems can cause stalling or a no-start.

causes.name: Failed crankshaft position sensor B
Damaged wiring or loose connector
Damaged tone ring or debris on the sensor tip
Engine computer fault

checks: Inspect the sensor's connector and wiring for oil, heat damage or chafing
Test the sensor signal with a scope before replacing it
fix: Usually a new crankshaft position sensor or a wiring repair.

title: Crankshaft Position Sensor "B" Circuit Range/Performance

title: Camshaft Position Sensor "B" Circuit (Bank 2)
plain: The engine computer says there's a fault in the circuit for camshaft position sensor B on bank 2. On most engines this sensor tracks the exhaust camshaft so the computer can time fuel, spark and valve timing.
symptoms: Stalling, rough running or reduced power

causes.name: Failed camshaft position sensor
Damaged wiring or loose, oil-soaked connector
Timing belt or chain stretched or jumped a tooth
Weak battery or charging voltage during cranking
Engine computer fault

checks: Inspect the sensor connector for oil, corrosion or a broken lock tab
Check battery and charging voltage
Compare cam and crank signals with a scan tool or scope to check timing
fix: Usually a new camshaft position sensor or a wiring repair; if the timing is off, the timing chain or belt needs attention.

fix: Start with the sensor and wiring, but this code often points to a stretched timing chain or cam phaser issue, which is a bigger job.
